original_question: Let A1A2...Am be a polygon and let P be a point inside it. Drop perpendiculars from P to each side AiAi+1, and let Ai' be the foot of the perpendicular on AiAi+1. The polygon A1'A2'...Am' is the pedal polygon of P. Determine what properties this pedal polygon must satisfy.
target_in_paper: Unsolved Problem 7.1: the paper asks for a polygonal generalization of Problem 7 by defining, for an interior point P of a polygon A_1...A_m, the pedal polygon A_1'...A_m' obtained from the perpendiculars from P to the sides A_iA_{i+1}, and then asking what properties that pedal polygon has. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official target very closely: it uses the same geometric setup as Unsolved Problem 7.1—namely a polygon A_1...A_m, an interior point P, perpendiculars from P to each side A_iA_{i+1}, the feet A_i', and the resulting pedal polygon A_1'A_2'...A_m'—and it asks for the properties of that pedal polygon. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))
missing_details: The paper frames this as a polygonal generalization of the immediately preceding triangle problem about the orthic triangle, so a fully paper-faithful stand-alone question should mention that local context. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))
The ambient setting is the Euclidean plane; the paper is not working in an abstract metric, projective, or non-Euclidean setting here. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))
Indices are cyclic, so the sides are A_iA_{i+1} with A_{m+1}=A_1. This is implicit in the notation of Unsolved Problem 7.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))
The paper explicitly calls P a pedal point, so that terminology should be included for maximum faithfulness. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))

The official wording is open-ended: it asks what properties the pedal polygon has, rather than asserting that there is a single universal condition it must satisfy. Your phrasing 'must satisfy' is slightly stronger than the paper's formulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))

The nearby motivation is Problem 7 and its conclusion on the orthic triangle of an acute triangle, including the derived inequality 4(a'b' + b'c' + c'a') <= a^2 + b^2 + c^2 and the extremal equilateral case; that context explains what kind of polygonal generalization the author has in mind. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))

The paper tacitly assumes that each perpendicular from P meets the side segment A_iA_{i+1} at A_i'; a stand-alone formulation should preserve that assumption in the definition of the pedal polygon. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))
refined_question: In the Euclidean plane, let A_1A_2...A_m be an m-gon (with indices taken modulo m), and let P be an interior point, called a pedal point. For each i, let A_i' be the foot of the perpendicular from P to the side A_iA_{i+1}; the polygon A_1'A_2'...A_m' is the pedal polygon of P. As the polygonal generalization of the orthic-triangle setting of Problem 7, determine what geometric properties this pedal polygon has. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Unsolved Problem 7.1, not nearby items 7.2 or 7.3, because it stays in the planar polygon setting and reproduces the exact pedal-polygon construction from perpendiculars to the sides. This also matches the paper's opening description that earlier 2D results are being extended from triangles to polygons or polyhedra. The immediate local context is Problem 7 and its conclusion about the orthic triangle of an acute triangle; Unsolved Problem 7.1 is posed directly afterward as the polygonal extension. Since the paper gives no explicit equivalent reformulation of 7.1, the safest refined version is a faithful, self-contained restatement of that open problem with its implicit Euclidean and cyclic-indexing setup made explicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))
